parsed.rationale: Although the two types share structural shape (both are `type-alias-object` with `shared_field_count: 1` and no declared fields), they carry distinct names — `TextHeightPreferenceKey` in `app:WatchXYC` (`WatchXYC/PlayerPage.swift:140`) and `ScrollOffsetPreferenceKey` in `app:iOS` (`iOS/Views/Playlist/Playcut Detail/PlaycutRowView.swift:74`) — and serve different UI measurement concerns in separate platform targets (watchOS vs. iOS). SwiftUI `PreferenceKey` conformances are typically small, boilerplate-heavy, and intentionally local to the view file that consumes them; merging them into a shared target would couple two unrelated platform UIs for no meaningful reduction in complexity. The structural similarity is purely coincidental, arising from the identical boilerplate shape of any `PreferenceKey` type alias rather than from shared domain logic.
